answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger resists Sybils by making each identity pay to exist. A new agent locks a deposit that vests slowly, like a glacier carving a valley: cheap to start, expensive to abandon and rebuild. Sybil farms face a dune of rising costs, since every fresh identity must fund its own bond and earn trust through attested work before it can vote or claim rewards. A jetty of rate-limited endorsements channels newcomers through verified peers, so a flood of fake accounts cannot wash over the system without first paying the bond and waiting out the vesting clock.
